name: Pikmin Bloom
tagline: Niantic's walking game where your real-world steps grow Pikmin, plant flowers on a shared map, and log your day as a picture diary.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Free download with coin packs and a paid subscription tier that has changed over time.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build a pedometer that grows cartoon plants, and it will be mildly satisfying for about four days. What you cannot build is a licensed Nintendo character, a live global map where millions of strangers' flower petals show up next to yours, or Niantic's decade of geospatial plumbing and background step tracking that survives iOS killing your app. The retention here is a licensed IP loop plus weekly community events plus the vague social pressure of a friend list, none of which a solo build has. A local step garden is a fine consolation project and an honest one, just do not pretend it is the same thing. Also worth noting: the game itself is free, so the DIY calculus is about ownership and taste, not saving money.
coreLoopDIY: A local-first phone web app that reads your daily step count, spends steps to grow procedurally generated seedlings, and drops a flower pin on a private map trail of where you walked.
requirements: A phone and a browser that exposes step or motion data (or an Apple Health / Google Fit export you import manually)
Location permission if you want the map trail
A place to host a PWA, or just run it on localhost over your LAN
whatYouLose: Pikmin. The actual characters are licensed Nintendo IP and you are not getting them
The shared world: other people's flowers, community events, Big Flower goals, friend lists
Reliable background step counting via native HealthKit and Google Fit, which a web app fakes badly
Niantic's map data and POI layer, so your map is a raw basemap with no sense of place
Art direction and animation polish that took a studio, not an afternoon
moatNotes: The Nintendo license is the part no amount of engineering skill routes around. Everything else is expensive but theoretically copyable.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays for Pikmin Bloom as a step tracker, they pay because it is Pikmin and because their walk to the shop turned into a shared flower streak with people they will never meet. The paid coins buy decor, expedition speedups, and storage, which are pure engagement taxes on a loop that only works because the characters are charming and the map is populated. A self-built version keeps the pedometer and loses the charm and the crowd, which is precisely the two things being purchased.
notes: A step-to-garden loop is a weekend build; Pikmin is not. The moat is a Nintendo license, a live global map of other people's flowers, and Niantic's geospatial stack.
prompt:
Build a local-first "step garden" progressive web app. No accounts, no backend, no analytics, no third party services.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage, MapLibre GL JS with a free raster basemap for the map view. Deploy target is a static build served over HTTPS on a phone, plus a working localhost dev flow.

Core loop:
1. Read step data. Primary path: DeviceMotionEvent accelerometer with a simple peak-detection step counter that runs while the app is foregrounded, plus a manual "add steps" input and a CSV importer for Apple Health / Google Fit exports so the data is not a lie when the app is closed. Be explicit in the UI about which source produced today's number.
2. Steps are currency. Every 200 steps matures one seedling. Seedlings are procedurally generated: seed a PRNG from the timestamp, derive petal count, two hex colors, stem curve, and a nonsense two-syllable species name. Render each plant as inline SVG, no image assets, no licensed characters.
3. Mature plants go into a Garden grid view, sortable by date and species, with a detail sheet showing the day and step count that grew it.
4. If location permission is granted, log a coarse GPS breadcrumb every 60 seconds while the app is open, and drop a flower marker on the MapLibre map at each point where a plant matured. Trail lines colored by day.
5. A Diary view: one card per day with total steps, plants grown, a distance estimate, and an optional user note plus an optional photo stored as a blob in IndexedDB.

Rules:
- All data stays in IndexedDB. Ship Export JSON and Import JSON buttons, and a Delete all data button that actually clears the database.
- Ship a manifest.json and a service worker so it installs to the home screen and works offline. Map tiles may fail offline; degrade to the Garden view without crashing.
- Mobile-first layout, thumb-reachable bottom tab bar with Today, Garden, Map, Diary.
- Seed the database with 14 days of fake history behind a dev-only "load demo data" button so the views are not empty on first run.
- No .env needed unless you choose a tile provider that requires a key; if so read it from VITE_MAP_KEY and document it in README.

Out of scope, do not build: friends, sharing, leaderboards, push notifications, any licensed characters or trademarked names, in-app purchases.

Finish with a README covering local dev, building, serving over HTTPS on a LAN so a phone can install it, the CSV import format, and a blunt note that foreground-only accelerometer counting undercounts real walking.
